what_happened: First pass inserted "enabled": false immediately after each of the 10 server openers in opencode.jsonc. The post-edit validator printed enabled=True for all 10 and `opencode mcp list` still showed every server connected. The change appeared to apply (script reported 'added to 10/10') but had no effect.
root_cause: Every server object already carried "enabled": true at its END. My insert went at the START. JSON duplicate-key resolution is last-wins, so the pre-existing true value overrode my false. I edited by anchored regex on the opener line and never read the remainder of the object, so I never saw the existing key.
what_i_did_wrong: I ran an edit against a JSON structure I had only partially inspected, and I trusted the tool's 'ADDED' success message as proof the semantic change landed. I only caught it because I re-parsed the file and re-ran `opencode mcp list` afterwards — the verification caught it, not the edit.
fix: Removed the 10 duplicate inserts, then flipped the 10 pre-existing flags from true to false, scoped strictly to the mcp block (mstart..mend offsets). Re-parsed JSON and re-ran `opencode mcp list`: 10 servers report 'disabled'.
actionable: When editing JSON/JSONC config by regex, read the whole target object first — duplicate keys are silent. Never treat an edit tool's 'APPLIED/ADDED' output as semantic proof; always re-parse and re-query the live system to confirm.
second_finding: My first attempt at disabling the 3 OMO builtins listed the 10 user server names in `disabled_mcps`. That key only feeds createBuiltinMcps() (oh-my-opencode-slim/dist/index.js:39863), so the list was inert. Root cause: I inferred the key's scope from its schema description ('MCP server names to disable completely') instead of reading the one call site. Corrected to [websearch, context7, gh_grep].
